reason: The text contains multiple human characters who demonstrate clear agency through their actions, speech, and decision-making. Moses and Aaron actively negotiate with Pharaoh, make strategic choices about what to communicate, and perform deliberate actions. Pharaoh exercises his own will by refusing requests, hardening his heart, issuing commands to his officials, and later calling for Moses to return. Egyptian officials and servants also act as agents—performing Pharaoh's commands and, at points in the narrative, advocating to their ruler. The Israeli people, while primarily affected by external circumstances, are portrayed as responding to situations (e.g., collecting straw, being compelled to work). All of these are depicted as regular human characters whose choices and actions drive portions of the narrative forward, despite the theological framework in which divine action ultimately governs outcomes.
